annotation.title_clean: Ghana (Country chapter: Insights on Public Policies to Ensure AI's Beneficial Use as a Professional Tool)
annotation.title_en: Ghana (Country chapter: Insights on Public Policies to Ensure AI's Beneficial Use as a Professional Tool)
annotation.venue: IBA Alternative and New Law Business Structures Committee
named_instruments_referenced: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of AI
annotation.summary_en: Ghana country chapter in an IBA survey on AI in legal services. It reports no statutory AI definition, no AI regulatory framework and no AI tools in legal practice. It notes that data protection law (Act 843), the constitutional privacy right and copyright law apply indirectly, and that the government and stakeholders see a need for an ethical and regulatory framework.
key_provisions_or_claims: Ghana has no statutory definition of AI and no AI-specific legal or regulatory framework.
Data Protection Act 2012 (Act 843) and constitutional privacy rights require consent for processing personal data used in AI.
Copyright Act 2005 (Act 690) protects software but has no express AI terms.
Legal profession rules contain no AI provisions; the lawyer's confidentiality duty applies.
Government and stakeholders have signalled a need for an ethical and regulatory AI framework.
